definitions.explanation: A parting greeting used when saying goodbye, especially when the separation may be for a long time or permanent. In everyday casual speech, shorter forms like じゃあね or バイバイ are more common.

examples.japanese: さよなら、⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧で⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧、⟦さようなら→さようなら：10531_sayounara⟧。
⟦{空港|くうこう}→空港：00648_kuukou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧さよなら⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}った→言う：00515_iu⟧とき、⟦{涙|なみだ}→涙：02235_namida⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: When I said goodbye to my friend at the airport, tears came to my eyes.

notes:
Despite being one of the most well-known Japanese words internationally, さよなら actually carries a sense of finality or long-term separation. Japanese speakers rarely use it for casual daily partings.

FORMS:
- ⟦さようなら→さようなら：10531_sayounara⟧ — the full, formal form
- さよなら — slightly shortened, the most common written form
- さよーなら — elongated casual form

USAGE:
- Used when children leave school: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧、⟦さようなら→さようなら：10531_sayounara⟧
- Used for emotional farewells (moving away, long trips, breakups)
- Can sound dramatic or final in everyday conversation

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦じゃあ→じゃあ：02989_jaa⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧ / ⟦じゃあまた→じゃあまた：22757_jaamata⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧ — see you later (casual, everyday)
- バイバイ — bye-bye (very casual, often used by younger people)
- ⟦では→では：02945_deha⟧ / ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ — well then (polite parting, used in business)
- {失礼|しつれい}します — excuse me, I'll be going (formal, workplace)
